name: Yush
streamSlot: Mon–Fri · 9:30 AM–12:00 PM ET · NY morning only
tagline: Ex-software engineer turned NQ/ES order-flow scalper — volume profile tells him where, delta and big trades tell him who's trapped.
summary: Yush is a former software engineer who trades NQ and ES futures full-time through prop firms (Lucid, Tradeify, Take Profit Trader, Apex and others) and a personal account, and says prop firms have paid him over $2M. After years of options losses and a year and a half on ICT concepts, he rebuilt his trading on Auction Market Theory, volume profile and order flow. He builds areas of interest from four tools — market-generated levels, the RTH volume profile, big trades (NQ 75+, ES 200+ lots) and the delta profile — and trades two models: look-above/below-and-fail at the value edges in balance, and pullbacks into low-volume nodes in trend. He trades only the New York morning, takes 2–3 trades a day, and never holds into news.
oneLiner: Map value with the volume profile, wait for price to reach an edge where two of four tools agree, then enter only when order flow shows absorption or trapped traders — fade failed breakouts in balance, buy LVN pullbacks in trend.
keyQuote: Most traders don't need another indicator. They need a read on who's trapped and a setup they can repeat.
highlights: An area of interest needs 2 of 4 tools — market levels, volume profile, big trades, delta profile
No return to the level, no trade — and never trade the middle of the range
Balance: look-above/below-and-fail at the value edge, enter on the reclaim, target the other side of value
Trend: let it break out, then enter the pullback into the low-volume node — never the breakout itself
Daily loss set before the open, split into 2–3 losing trades — the last one ends the day
Average up, never down; never let a winning trade go red

videos.title: Read Market Structure Like A PRO (Auction Market Theory
videos.takeaway: Auction Market Theory from zero: price moves until one side stops showing up. Excess vs poor highs, balance vs imbalance, and the three morning questions — where is value, are we opening inside or outside it, is the new price accepted or rejected.

videos.title: Trading Was Hard Until I Stopped Reading Candlesticks
videos.takeaway: What's inside a candle: every trade has a buyer and seller, price moves on urgency (aggressive market orders vs passive limits). Level 1 vs Level 2 vs order flow, and why he now uses candles only as a clock.

videos.title: Live Trading NQ & ES Futures | Order flow
videos.takeaway: Choppy gap-down session at monthly lows: sets a hard daily loss limit and no profit target, quits a range after being chopped in it, skips an LAF whose value area was too narrow for 2R, and wins back the day on an LBF at the developing VAL with zero-gamma confluence.

videos.title: Would you buy or sell? #trading #daytrading #orderflow #volumeprofile
videos.takeaway: Buy-or-sell quiz: price breaks under VAL, a big negative delta bar prints with no follow-through, enter on the close back above VAL, stop just below, target VAH — an LBF.

videos.title: How to trade FVG with orderflow #trading #daytrading
videos.takeaway: Trading an FVG with order flow: treat it as a low-volume node, wait for the pullback, and require proof — aggression, absorption or trapped traders — before entering; stop beyond the LVN, target the prior high.

videos.title: The Ultimate Guide to Orderflow Delta Profile
videos.takeaway: Delta = ask volume minus bid volume — it measures aggression, not 'more buyers'. How the delta profile shows absorption (aggression with no result), aligned aggression that gets paid, and trapped traders at the value edges.

videos.title: This one orderflow strategy has made me over $200,000 from one prop firm #daytrading #futurestrading
videos.takeaway: The look-below-and-fail setup explained: breakout sellers FOMO under VAL, big buyers absorb them, the candle closes back above VAL — enter, stop under the swing low, target the other side of balance and VAH.

videos.title: Live Trading NQ & ES Futures | Order flow | yushcapital.co

videos.title: How I Made $3,000 on Nasdaq Using Orderflow & GEX

videos.title: Don't Miss This Nasdaq Absorption Pattern
videos.takeaway: Reading absorption with big trades + delta profile: the first stall gets your attention, the second failed push confirms, the third sweep of the highs that fails is the entry — trapped buyers fuel the break of structure.

videos.title: How I Made $3,400 Trading the GEX Levels

articles.title: Yush's Strategy: Trading Trapped Buyers & Sellers with Order Flow (Chart Fanatics)
articles.takeaway: Full written strategy: AOIs need 2 of 4 tools (market levels, volume profile, big trades NQ 75+/ES 200+, delta profile). Model 1 range — fade only the edges, TP1 midpoint then opposite value, breakeven after TP1. Model 2 trend — enter LVN pullbacks, scale into strength. 2–3 trades a day, never trade into momentum.

articles.title: 74% Win Rate Trader Shares His EXACT OrderFlow Strategy ($2M+ Payouts) — Chart Fanatics interview
articles.takeaway: Whiteboard walk-through of the four AOI tools and both models, aggressive vs confirmation entries, value migration as 'a big part of my edge', never trading breakouts or into momentum, and a live NY session.

articles.title: He Switched ICT Concepts For OrderFlow And Made $2M+ in Payouts — PropFirmTrader
articles.takeaway: Rules over setups: the daily loss limit is the rule that saved him the most money, stop after 2–3 losses, bench a firm after a red day, one contract per $1K of buffer, and 'most prop traders fail from expectations, not risk'.

articles.title: TOP Ranked Futures Prop Trader with $2+ Million in Payouts — Words of Rizdom
articles.takeaway: His story from software engineer to prop trader, why order flow gave the confirmation ICT never did, no cross-firm copy trading, eval spending caps, no edge in Asia, and building a skill that transfers to live markets.

articles.title: The $17M+ Prop Firm Roundtable — Words of Rizdom
articles.takeaway: Roundtable with other funded traders: risking 15–20 NQ points for 40–50+, adding to winners on micros, confidence-based sizing, vetting new prop firms, and 'a loss is just a pullback for new highs'.
